value.name: FGCU Salutes Service and Sacrifice Week
value.description:
FGCU America 250: Service & Sacrifice Week is a powerful week-long celebration honoring the men and women who have served—and continue to serve—our nation. From November 9–13, Florida Gulf Coast University will bring together students, faculty, staff, veterans, active-duty service members, reservists, military families, community leaders, and partners for a meaningful series of events recognizing 250 years of American service, courage, and sacrifice.

 

Throughout the week, attendees will experience military traditions, inspiring stories, patriotic ceremonies, demonstrations, community partnerships, and opportunities to connect with those who have dedicated their lives to protecting our freedoms. Whether you have worn the uniform, supported someone who has, or simply value the freedoms we share, Service & Sacrifice Week is an opportunity for the entire FGCU community to come together, remember our history, honor those who served, and celebrate the legacy we carry forward. Join us as we proudly honor 250 years of service and sacrifice—and the people who made it possible.

 

A Week of Recognition and Remembrance

Monday, November 9 – Army Day
The week will begin with a celebration of the United States Army, recognizing its history and contributions to our nation's defense. Activities will highlight Army traditions, leadership, service, and the connection between military service and higher education. Model A and Model T Club will celebrate event day with us.

Monday- 1000AM Color Guard Ceremony in COHEN 201, National Anthem and Pledge of Allegiance.

1100-4PM Military Vehicles outside of COHEN , Visit Business Vendors and Military Recruiters , Vendors in COHEN 201 , Military Museum Items in COHEN 214 and Much More!!

Tuesday, November 10 – Veterans Day Celebration
FGCU will host its primary Veterans Day Celebration and Flag-Folding Ceremony at the Veterans Pavilion, including recognition of veterans and service members, patriotic music, remarks from university and community leaders, and the ceremonial folding of the American flag. The ceremony will provide an opportunity to reflect on the meaning of service, sacrifice, duty, and freedom.

Wednesday, November 11 – Veterans Day & FGCU Athletics Recognition
FGCU Athletics will recognize veterans and military members during a home athletic event. A military color guard, national anthem, and recognition activities will help bring the university and Southwest Florida communities together in honoring those who have served.

Thursday, November 12 – Military & Veterans Community Expo
FGCU will host a large-scale Military and Veterans Expo featuring community organizations, veteran service providers, military organizations, government agencies, employers, and educational partners. The event will provide students and veterans with opportunities to connect with resources, services, employment, education, and community support.

 

Friday, November 13 – Grand Recognition
The week will conclude with a Grand Recognition Ceremony celebrating veterans, military families, ROTC cadets, service organizations, and community partners. The event will emphasize the enduring relationship between FGCU and the Southwest Florida military community.

 

More Than a Celebration

Service & Sacrifice is designed to be more than a Veterans Day observance. It represents FGCU's commitment to building a lasting culture of military and veteran inclusion, education, leadership, and community engagement.

Through partnerships with local governments, veteran organizations, military units, community agencies, and supporters throughout Southwest Florida, FGCU seeks to create a meaningful platform where the stories of service are remembered, sacrifices are honored, and future generations are inspired to serve.

The week also provides an opportunity to showcase FGCU's growing Military and Veterans Success initiatives, ROTC development, student veteran support, community partnerships, and commitment to those who have worn the uniform.

Our Message

We remember those who served.
We honor those who sacrificed.
We support those who continue to serve.
And we inspire the next generation to lead.

Service & Sacrifice: America 250 Military Commemoration
Florida Gulf Coast University | November 9–13, 2026

value.name: Etiquette Dinner ( Now on a Wait List Only)
value.description:
Etiquette Dinner - Closed

Tuesday, November 3  |  5 p.m. – 7:30 p.m.  |  Sponsored by Enterprise Holdings

Free food, real skills, and a room full of people who want to help you succeed. The Etiquette Dinner walks you through how to handle yourself at a formal business or interview dinner — the kind of situation that trips up a lot of new professionals. You will practice networking in a relaxed setting, learn the etiquette rules that matter, and walk away more confident going into any professional setting. It is one of the most practical events we offer, and it will not cost you a thing. Professional dress is required and you must register in advance.

Good for: All students, especially those heading into interview season or internship recruiting.

📅 Register on Eagle Career Network or Eagle Link — professional dress required. 

 

*Gold Career Ready Approved Event*

value.description:

*Gold Career Ready Cord Approved Event*

value.name: Arthrex Expo
value.description:
Arthrex Expo

Tuesday, November 17  |  10 a.m. – 2 p.m.

Arthrex is one of the most well-known and respected companies in Southwest Florida — and this event opens the door for any student, from any major, to learn what a career there looks like. Engineering, business, marketing, IT, operations, finance — there are opportunities across the board. Stop by, talk to employees from different departments, ask honest questions, and see if it feels like the right fit. You might be surprised what you find.

Good for: All students and alumni — no specific major required.

📅 No advance registration required. Just show up.

value.name: Hatter Tournament Fall 2026
value.description:

value.name: Keynote: Empower Students to Write Their Own Success Stories
value.description:
Student success is more than picking a major or visiting the career office. It’s about the whole degree.

The PAGES Program present Ned Laff and Scott Carlson, authors of Hacking College, Why the Major Doesn't Matter - and What Really Does, who will explain how students can turn the grab bag of courses and activities into a coherent field of study that supports their individual career goals. The lecture will both informative and lively. 

 

Ned Laff has over 35 years of expertise in helping students craft successful undergraduate experiences that supported their career goals or significantly improved their chances for admissions to graduate school. Past projects include developing Columbia College's Carnegie Foundation for Civic Engagement recognition, continual recognition from the Corporation for National and Community Service with the Presidential Honors Designation, and helping Governors State University being named one of 5 colleges and universities to be recognized by the Washington Center with their 2012 Civic Engagement Award.

 

Scott Carlson is a Senior writer and columnist at The Chronicle of Higher Education and primarily writes about where higher education is headed, how it serves (or doesn't serve) students and the public, and how the sector can stay relevant and resilient.

value.name: Resume Workshop w/ Career Development Services
value.description: Join the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM) in partnership with Career Development Services (CDS) for an interactive Resume Workshop designed to help you turn campus experiences, leadership roles, and coursework into interview-winning resumes. In this hands-on session, career specialists will guide you through  standards, strategic formatting, and the art of crafting quantifiable, impact-driven bullet points that capture recruiters' attention. Whether you are building your first draft for upcoming internships or refining an existing resume for post-grad opportunities, bring your laptop and current draft to gain the practical tools, live feedback, and competitive edge needed to stand out in today's job market.
